title: Inside the twisting box (E3 in depth)
learning_goal: See how the 3D solver is validated, what the dominant mode looks like, and how precise the thresholds are: the provenance of Bet 1, and the question to settle before the 64³ runs.
takeaway: The 3D test bench passes an exact check and recovers the known windows, with honest limits on precision.
notes: Extension module, extended cut only, inserted after X5a (that is, after X5a.Q; CONTRACT P1) and before 10.4, whose Bet 1 it sets up: the 32³ curve, its exact check and its uncertainty (critique I1). Four scenes: X1.1, X1.2, X1.3 ready (as the outline) and one NEW question card X1.Q. Register NIGHT throughout (X5a ends on NIGHT, 10.4 is NIGHT). Modules are asides: no chapter card; X1.1 carries the rail at L4 and the lower-third tag 'EXTENSION X1 · LEVEL 4 · AN ASIDE' in its 0.6-s lead-in. Badges: MEASURED on the three scenes (E3), none on the card; X1.2 also says two published CONTEXT facts, each with a reference lower-third and an external source. Narration never says 'E3', 'lambda', 'eigenmode' or 'Beltrami' (on screen only); it says 'the long fit' and 'the late fit', the same words as 10.4, and 'Bet one' as 10.4. SYMBOLS: s and s_q for the two fits (never λ; the report's λ and λ_q), Rm green, B vermillion, u blue, generator violet; η appears only inside \etaP on the formula layer. CHANGES AGAINST THE OUTLINE, to review. (1) X1.3 target 35 -> 50 s (45 by the writer, 50 after review): a predict beat ('right on the edge: same sign?', hold 2.5 s), the probable cause of the imprecision (oscillating modes, R:1114) said aloud because the card follows from it, the divergence gauge narrated, and a closing bridge to Bet 1. (2) NEW question card X1.Q (category runs, ask Y. Ponty / C. Nore): fit growth with an oscillation term, or run longer? It unblocks t_keep of palier2_abc3d (hence its GPU hours) and the estimator behind Bet 1's verdict rule (ln‖B‖ is already logged every 0.5 time unit, enough for either estimator); it is distinct from the 10.4 seat's ASK (extra points at Rm 17.25, 17.5, 17.75, D17). Module 1:55 -> 2:24 after review (38 + 47 + 50 + 9 s; the writer had 35 + 45 + 45 + 9 at about 135 effective words per minute). (3) X1.1 follows B8 strictly: the exact mode is a lower bound; the narration says 'on the bound to about one part in ten thousand' (|−0.500053 + 0.5| / 0.5 = 1.1e-4) and the magnifier shows that the long fit sits a hair below the bound (5.3e-5), by about the gap between the two fits (4.6e-5): within the fit's own accuracy. (4) X1.2 narrates a READING of the stored modes that the report does not state: at Rm 8, 16 and 20 the field gathers in four slim tubes along the cube's diagonals, peaking exactly on four of the eight stagnation points of the flow; at Rm 12 it is broader. After review the narration frames this as 'in these snapshots' (each stored field is one instant, t = 150; the report says the first-window modes oscillate, so a shape may depend on the phase). Checked read-only on experiences/resultats/e3_modes.npz (no run); the extractor must write these values into data/X1_modes3d.json so that the claim is traceable; the matching literature (cigar-like tubes in the classical A = B = C dynamo, Archontis, Dorch & Nordlund 2003, already in the report's bibliography; Dorch 2000) is a sourced CONTEXT fact. If the lead prefers report-only claims, replace X1.2.s6-s8 by 'In these snapshots, at eight, sixteen and twenty, the strong field gathers in a few slim tubes; at twelve, it spreads out.' and drop the stagnation rings. DATA. X1.1 and X1.3: data/e3_growth.json (exists). X1.2: NEW data/X1_modes3d.json, READY content for tools/data_existing.py (converter 'x1_modes3d', content listed at the end of X1.2 'visual'): precomputed isosurfaces and field lines (critique G8), the stagnation points and |B| there, the blob summary. data/e3_modes.json (32³ |B|, 16³ components) is NOT enough for G8-quality lines; it stays the source of the 03.4 insets. REQUEST to foundation engineer B: in tools/data_existing.py:353 the series name 's, 32³ (whole run)' is wrong: s is fitted over the SECOND HALF of each run (R:1066; experiences/e3_abc.py:85-86); rename it 's, 32³ (second half)'. 03.4 does not show the name; 10.4's pictogram label 'long fit · whole kept window' is fine for the 64³ campaign but its ghost legend should not say 'whole run'. LEXICON: 'Rm' and 'ABC' already pinned; no new entry ('cigar-shaped', 'Bet one', 'three-dimensional' are plain English). MUSIC: none (L4). PACE: words budgeted at 125-130 effective words per minute against target_s; estimates with the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in, tail). REVIEW 2026-11-08 (script/_review/X1.md): X1.1 no longer ties the cancellation of carrying and stretching to the corkscrew (u × B = u × u = 0 holds for B = u in ANY flow; the Beltrami property only makes diffusion keep the shape, ∇²u = −u); 'dominant rate' replaced by 'the measured rate, the slowest fade'; X1.2 hedged to the stored snapshots, 'peaking at points' (4 of the 8), 'proposed' not 'planned' (R:1218 is a proposal); X1.3 predict beat made explicit and lengthened, 'about a tenth' read as 'zero point one'; X1.Q 'unblocks' no longer claims the logging cadence drives GPU hours. Pace re-budgeted at 127.5-130 effective words per minute. CONSISTENCY EDITOR (2026-11-08): X1.Q numbered Q17 (register numbering).

box_icon.what: the 2D icon of the twisting box used in 03.4 and 10.4 (grey cube outline, three --u corkscrew strokes)

sentences.text: Before trusting the solver, test it on a known answer.
The twisting {u}flow{/} offers one: a {b}field{/} shaped exactly like it.
Its lines follow the flow's own lines, so carrying and stretching cancel.
Only diffusion acts: its growth rate is exactly minus one over {param}Rm{/}.
So the measured rate, the slowest fade, can be no lower: at {param}Rm{/} two, minus one half.
The solver finds minus zero point five zero zero one, on the bound to about one part in ten thousand.

labels: carried and stretched by the flow
the dominant rate cannot be here

formulas.tex: \text{an exact mode decays at } -1/\Rm \;\Rightarrow\; s_{\text{dominant}}(\Rm) \ge -1/\Rm;\qquad \Rm = 2:\ s_{\text{dominant}} \ge -0.5

chips: on the bound to about 1 part in 10⁴ · the two fits differ by 5 × 10⁻⁵

On 'copy-0.15': in the left panel a 7 x 7 lattice of --u arrows: the in-plane components (u_x, u_y) = (cos y, 1 + sin x) of the ABC flow on the slice z = 0, computed in setup from the closed form with A, B, C read from ctx.data.e3.config, length proportional to the in-plane speed (at most 70 px); plain chip 'slice z = 0 · in-plane arrows' under the panel. Then a --b copy of every arrow slides in from 30 px to the right and lands on its blue twin, offset 4 px so both inks stay visible (0.6 s each, outCubic, 30-ms stagger in the seeded order Scene.rng('x1-copy')); label '{b}B{/} = {u}u{/}' (Kit.markup, 44 px) above the lattice. On 'fade-0.15': the pen boxes 'diff', label 'diffusion only · shape kept' (the Beltrami property, ∇²u = −u, is on the formula layer); under the equation the result 's = −1/Rm' writes on (KaTeX, Rm green via \Rm); in the lattice the vermillion arrows shrink together to 40 % of their length over 2.5 s (outCubic), keeping every direction, while the blue arrows stay: same shape, smaller; plain chip 'time compressed · shape exact'. P2. On 'bound-0.15': the right panel draws the rate ruler (params.ruler): a horizontal axis 's, growth rate' from −0.6 to 0.1, ticks −0.6 to 0 every 0.1 (Kit.fmt, U+2212 minus); a green chip 'Rm = 2' (from exact_check.Rm) above its left end; a chalk tick at exact_check.bound labelled 'exact mode: −1/Rm = −0.5'; the zone left of it (s < −0.5) hatched grey (45-degree lines, 25 % opacity) with the label 'the dominant rate cannot be here'. The answer slot of P1 now reads 'dominant rate ≥ −0.5'. On 'measure-0.15': a --b drop-pin falls from y 260 onto the ruler and settles at exact_check.s (−0.500053) with Scene.spring (overshoot at most 3 %), label 'measured: −0.5001' (Kit.fmt(s, 4)); 'pop' when it lands (sfx). At 'measure+1.2' a circular magnifier (params.magnifier, radius 150 px, centre x 1380, y 540) opens under the ruler, tied to −0.5 by two thin grey lines: inside, a zoomed axis from −0.5002 to −0.4999 (ticks −0.5002, −0.5001, −0.5000, −0.4999) with the chalk exact tick at −0.5, a filled --b dot at the long fit (exact_check.s, label 'long fit · second half') and an open --b dot at the late fit (ctx.data.e3.series[1].y[0] = −0.500007, label 'late fit · last quarter'); under the magnifier the plain chip 'on the bound to about 1 part in 10⁴ · the two fits differ by 5 × 10⁻⁵' (both numbers computed from the data with Kit.fmt, never typed). At 'measure+2.4' the pen (kind 'check') ticks the answer slot. Source lower-third (Kit.lowerThird kind 'source', data ctx.data.e3, at 'measure+0.4', hold 5; the module tag is long gone). Badge MEASURED with the script's note. Formula layer (Kit.formulaLayer(ctx), label 'Formula · R:1116, R:1066'). Key colours: blue (u), vermillion (B, s), green (Rm, η): three, never a fourth; everything else grey and chalk. No corner needle (no dipole on screen). Idle motion: the lattice breathes (arrow length ±2 %, 4-s period) whenever nothing else moves; the pin never moves after it lands.

AS BUILT (2026-11-08, batch 4): flat SVG + KaTeX. Lattice of in-plane ABC arrows at z = 0 from the closed form (A, B, C from e3_growth config) with the vermillion copies landing on them; the 03.1 equation as a callback (size 56), 'adv' struck, 'diff' boxed; s = −1/Rm; the copies shrink to 40 %; ruler with the bound, the hatched forbidden zone, the spring pin at exact_check.s; magnifier (moved to x 1580, y 620, r 110) with the long and late fits; the legend of the two dots and the precision line are labels in the right panel (all numbers from the file: relative gap → '1 part in 10⁴', fit difference → '5 × 10⁻⁵'). sentences.text: Run long enough, and one {b}field{/} takes over: the slowest to fade, or the fastest to grow.
The surface wraps its strong parts; threads trace its lines.
At {param}Rm{/} eight, it fades.
At twelve and sixteen, inside the window, it grows.
At twenty, just past it, it fades again.
In these snapshots, at eight, sixteen and twenty, it gathers in four slim tubes.
They peak at points where the {u}flow{/} stands still.
At twelve, it spreads out.
Published work describes such cigar-shaped tubes, and symmetries the report did not check.
One shape per setting: proposed first targets for a three-dimensional {model}generator{/}.

labels: {model}generator{/} targets · one per Rm · proposed next step

scenes.title: How sure are the thresholds?

badge.note: E3 · 32³ and two 48³ checks · fits over the second half and the last quarter

long.label: long fit · second half
long.note: the file labels series[0] 'whole run': wrong, it is the second-half fit (R:1066, e3_abc.py:85-86); never show the file's name

sentences.text: How precise are those edges? Each run gets a long fit over its second half, a late fit over its last quarter.
A finer grid rechecks two settings. At {param}Rm{/} twelve, all three agree.
At seventeen and a half, right on the edge: same sign?
No: the long fit says growing; the late fit and finer grid, fading.
This edge is known to about zero point one; the third, near twenty-seven, to about one.
A likely cause, still unchecked: the modes oscillate, so the growth curve wobbles.
The divergence, at least, stays at rounding error.
That unresolved sign is where Bet one begins.

\text{thresholds } (32^{3},\ \text{linear interpolation of } s):\ 8.87,\ 17.6\ (\pm 0.1),\ 26.8\ (\pm 1);\ \text{published } 8.9,\ 17.5,\ \approx 27;\ \ |s - s_q| \text{ up to } 2.2\times10^{-3} \text{ for } 20 \le \Rm \le 26\ (\text{at } \Rm = 20 \text{ and } 26)
\text{published (Bouya \& Dormy 2013): first-window modes oscillate, } \omega \approx 0.53 \;\Rightarrow\; \ln\|\B\| \approx s\,t + \text{oscillation}\ \ (\text{cause not verified})
\|\nabla\cdot\B\|_{\mathrm{rel}} \in [3\times10^{-19},\ 1.52\times10^{-16}] \text{ over the 24 runs: curl form, } \mathbf k\cdot(\mathbf k\times\hat{\mathbf v}) = 0

question.en: Near the thresholds, should we fit growth rates with an *oscillation term*, or simply run *longer*?
question.say: Near the thresholds, should we fit growth rates with an oscillation term, or simply run longer?
question.fr: Près des seuils, faut-il ajuster les taux de croissance avec un *terme d'oscillation*, ou simplement simuler *plus longtemps* ?
question.why: At 32³ the long and late fits split at the second and third edges, probably because the modes oscillate (published, not verified here); Bet 1 is judged on those two fits agreeing.
question.unblocks: Runs: how long the 64³ ABC campaign keeps each Rm (t_keep, now 100 time units after 150 of transient, about eight periods at the published ω ≈ 0.53), hence its GPU hours; ln‖B‖ is already logged every 0.5 time unit, enough for either estimator. Framing: the growth-rate estimator, and the verdict rule of Bet 1.
question.why_fr: À 32³, l'ajustement long et l'ajustement tardif divergent aux deuxième et troisième seuils, sans doute parce que les modes oscillent (publié, non vérifié ici) ; le pari 1 est jugé sur l'accord de ces deux ajustements.
question.unblocks_fr: Simulations : combien de temps la campagne ABC à 64³ garde chaque Rm (t_keep, aujourd'hui 100 unités de temps après 150 de transitoire, environ huit périodes à la pulsation publiée ω ≈ 0,53), donc ses heures GPU ; ln‖B‖ est déjà enregistré toutes les 0,5 unité de temps, assez pour l'un ou l'autre estimateur. Cadrage : l'estimateur du taux de croissance et la règle de verdict du pari 1.
